question.worked_solution:
We multiply out the parentheses and then use the identity $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{cot}⁡x(3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\operatorname{csc}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot 3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot 2\operatorname{csc}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot 3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot 2\operatorname{csc}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (3\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x-2\int \operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2(-\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+C \\  & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\operatorname{csc}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$
